answers.value: Universal liquid glass for 3D objects in TouchDesigner 2025.x (GLSL 4.60, macOS Apple Silicon); glass colour and reflection, translucency, opacity, overall style; no dithering; presets (menu loads editable values, plus A/B morph); separate Refraction and Reflection TOPs; tutorial for TD users new to GLSL.

Vertex displacement by an animated object-space liquid field with rebuilt normals; the core pixel stage and presets unchanged; crack-free mode; tessellation, non-uniform scale and instancing documented.
Away from centre (crack-free), because tearing is an outright artefact on common hard-edged meshes, while weaker motion on non-star-shaped meshes is milder. Normal mode is one menu choice away.
Amplitude as a fraction of Object size, scales in features per object size, measured from Flow centre, so presets transfer between objects.
Each of the 12 core presets keeps its look values and gains a motion character (for example Sapphire Drop sags into drops, Chrome Type carries travelling waves, Liquid Mercury swells fast).
A sphere by default (the blob of reference 3), with torus, box (crack test) and grid (open sheet) on a menu.
TouchDesigner 2025.x, GLSL 4.60, macOS Apple Silicon. Not available here; native checks pending.
studies/liquid-glass-flow/ (self-contained).
The workflow brief asked to verify and fix 14 reviewer findings without asking questions; the choices below are inferences within that brief.

Speed added up per frame in the presets module, advanced by the uniform expression, rather than a Speed CHOP (32-bit samples stall slow speeds once the sum is large) or an Execute DAT writing a parameter every frame. Pause gives Fixed time x speed, so paused looks are unchanged.
Gravity now includes each instance's rotation and scale (TDInstanceMat3), which answers the earlier open question: sagging drops point down in the world.
A pulse button, not live expressions: one material can serve several objects, and an expression would refit whenever the SOP changes. Not run at build time; the defaults already fit the demo sphere.
Documented with measured numbers rather than capping Amplitude, because a cap would also limit crack-free mode, whose normals are exact.
Six grid faces merged, matching the preview and keeping split normals along the edges, instead of a divided Box SOP, which Derivative documents as not rendering.

Sync this member with the core: rebase the pixel stage on the core working tree after its family-sync merge, bring the core's audit rounds 2 and 3 (R1 to R9) and the family merge items (C1 to C9) where they apply, keep the member's own identity and better solutions, use the plugin's skill files, no questions.

advance() everywhere (per-component state, no absTime in expressions, holds at speed 0); this study's folded drift kept for the vertex field (one flow time wrapped at 25600). Comparison in decisions.json.

Flow fit > Object size (renamed from Flowsize to the core's internal name Objectsize) also scales the glass lengths, in SOP units; no second size control. A scaled Geometry COMP leaves the glass lengths at the unscaled size (documented).

open_questions: Does the user prefer Normal mode as the default for their own meshes (smooth, open surfaces)? Its normals are approximate (up to 10 degrees on the demo torus).
Should Fit to Glass geometry also run automatically when Glass geometry changes?
Should experiments keep Faces and Displace along as setup controls instead, with the demo experiments that need them moved to a second component?
LOOK-F1 (look_decisions_for_user): which default Object size should the demo use? The radius-1.45 sphere this question first offered does not keep the old look; it renders today's (measured there).

Family critic: should Object size switch to SOP units, with the shader following the Geometry COMP's scale and each instance's scale by itself (decisions.json, Family critic: one Object size per component, option (b))? It would make animated and per-instance scale work without Fit, but changes what a typed Object size means on a scaled COMP, in every member.

Family open question (centre-line residual): with antialiasing, a few silhouette pixels near the render's centre row or column still take the wrong screen orientation, so they bend the wrong way. In the WebGL preview each member's survey finds up to 8 of them per row of twelve renders; in the final image they change at most 7 pixels per row, by up to 43/255 in an emulated flipped raster and up to 38/255 in TouchDesigner's usual one. Are they visible in TouchDesigner? The native check centre_line_residual (validation.json, family_close.native_run) answers it. If they are, try a centroid-qualified vertex output for the projected position in Liquid Glass Lit first (form (e) of Lit's survey), then bring it to the core and the other members. Until then no member changes its shader for it.

look_decisions_for_user.how_to_answer: Asked through the host's question tool, one decision per question with the recommended option first. In a host without a question tool, answer in text by naming a decision and an option, for example 'LOOK-F1 B'. Each option says what it changes. Until you answer, the code stays as delivered.
look_decisions_for_user.rule: Until the user answers, the option in the code stays there: checks/test_study.py, LookDecisions, fails if it changes. After an answer, record it here (origin user, with the user's words), change the code, set in_code to the chosen option and update that test's IN_CODE and its check of the code.

decisions.question: Which default Object size should the demo use?
decisions.what_changed: The family close set the default Object size to 1 / 1.45 (0.69), what Fit sets on the radius-1 demo sphere. Before, it was 1. On the demo the glass is now thinner relative to the sphere, so it bends, magnifies, frosts and tints less, and its ripples and film bands are 1.45 times finer. Against c94e849 the 12 preset captures changed by 99 to 241/255 and the 16 motion frames by 213 to 249/255 (max per channel).

options.A: Keep 0.69 (in the code now). The demo shows the core's presets at the size they were tuned for on the core's torus, and Fit changes nothing on the demo. No code change.
options.B: Go back to a default of 1. The demo looks as at c94e849, but pressing Fit on the demo sets 0.69 and the look jumps to A's. Changes: the default and label in study.json, the tests and captures that assume 0.69.
options.C: Keep 0.69 and give Flow its own copy of the twelve presets, with Thickness, Frost and Scene depth x 1.45, Tint density / 1.45 and Wobble scale / 1.45 (as Prism did for its own looks). Lengths and ripples look as at c94e849 and Fit changes nothing, but the film bands stay 1.45 times finer (the family rule fixes the film count), and the presets no longer equal the core's: the same preset name gives a different look than in Liquid Glass on the same object. Changes: presets.json, test_core_looks_unchanged and amplitude0_matches_core (compared at converted values), captures.

decisions.recommended_origin: inference (the look-acceptance round, 2026-11-02; the user has not answered)
decisions.why_recommended: Universality first. With A, one Object size means the same glass in every member, Fit is a no-op on the demo, and Flow's presets stay the core's. B makes the default disagree with Fit; C splits the presets from the core's. If the stronger bend of the reference images is wanted, a thicker preset reaches it without either cost.
decisions.not_an_option: Scaling the demo sphere to radius 1.45 at Object size 1 (Flow size 1.45, camera 1.45 times farther). The earlier open question offered it as a way to keep the old look. Measured, it renders today's look (at most 4/255 from it, 0 pixels over 8/255), not c94e849's (222 to 242/255 from it): lengths follow the object, so a bigger sphere at a bigger Object size looks the same (checks/results/look-decisions.json, option_radius_1_45).
